nodes.description: Contract state array `newParents` holding 29 hard-coded parent addresses that are pushed into the external elixor contract.
Contract state array `newChildren` holding 29 hard-coded child addresses passed to the external elixor contract.
Public function `addGenesisPairs()` (acts as constructor of contract addGenesisPairs). It writes the literal address arrays into storage and then calls into an external contract.
`importGenesisPairs(address[] newParents, address[] newChildren)` declared in contract `elixor`; the externally invoked function at a hard-coded address.
Local variable `elixorContract`, an `elixor` handle created by casting the literal address 0x898bF3...cBc53; used as the call target.
External call `elixorContract.importGenesisPairs(newParents,newChildren)` to an attacker-influencable/deployed contract, executed after the state arrays are populated.

edges.reason: Function func_addGenesisPairs writes the literal parent address list into state variable newParents.
Function func_addGenesisPairs writes the literal child address list into state variable newChildren.
State variable newParents is read and passed as the first argument of the external call.
State variable newChildren is read and passed as the second argument of the external call.
Local variable elixorContract supplies the destination address/interface for the external call performed on line with importGenesisPairs.
Execution of func_addGenesisPairs invokes the external call unsafe operation.

The external call transfers control to the untrusted code at the elixor address, which re-enters/executes importGenesisPairs; the target is attacker-controllable, enabling reentrancy-style interaction rather than a trusted self-call.

normalization_plan.reason: The local variable elixorContract is only a temporary handle used to build the call target parameter; it has no independent semantics and is merged into the external call unsafe operation it feeds.
